chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever prays salat outside of its prescribed time, there is no salat for him.

key_terms.صلاة: The ritual prayer (salat), one of the pillars of Islam; here used both for the act of praying and the validity of that prayer
key_terms.فلا صلاة له: Negation formula meaning the act is legally null and void, carrying no religious merit
key_terms.وقت: The prescribed time window for each of the five daily prayers, as determined by the position of the sun

ai.seo_question: What happens if you pray salat outside its prescribed time according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a decisive legal ruling: prayer performed outside its prescribed time is legally invalid and does not count. This ruling addresses the importance of observing the exact time windows (awqat) for each of the five daily prayers, which the Quran (4:103) explicitly states are fixed obligations. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith supports the position that intentionally delaying prayer beyond its prescribed window requires qada (makeup prayer) and carries legal consequences.
